E01 & Does the building automation system control the \{heating/\allowbreak{}cooling\} and/\allowbreak{}or lighting? Heating? /\allowbreak{} Cooling? & T+\allowbreak{}Sp+\allowbreak{}SAT+\allowbreak{}Run & 19 of 45 & all three & A BAS that controls heating or cooling reads zone temperature and setpoints, and the supply-air temperature and run status of the systems it commands. Supply-air temperature presumes an air system; hydronic-only buildings would not carry it. \\
E02 & Does the building automation system control ... lighting? & Occ & 2 of 45 & sensitivity only & BAS lighting control taken as occupancy-driven. As a sensitivity only: a BAS that only schedules lighting would carry no occupancy stream; CBECS does not separate the two. \\
E03 & Occupancy sensors that reduce lighting when rooms are unoccupied? & Occ & 2 of 45 & all three & Lighting occupancy sensors are usually local devices with no network point. \\
E04 & Does this building use any `smart' or internet-connected thermostats? & T+\allowbreak{}Sp & 23 of 45 & all three & An internet-connected thermostat exposes zone temperature and setpoint. Asked only of buildings without a BAS, so the row cannot fire in BAS buildings. \\
E05 & Lighting scheduling (lights automatically dimmed or turned off at certain times)? & none & — & all three & A time schedule adds no stream class. \\
E06 & Multi-level lighting or dimming? & none & — & all three & A dimming device adds no stream class. \\
E07 & Demand controlled ventilation (DCV)? & CO$_2$ & 1 of 45 & all three & Demand-controlled ventilation taken as CO$_2$-based (90.1 \S{}6.4.3.8 also allows occupancy-based demand-controlled ventilation). \\
E08 & Daylight harvesting (automatically dims light fixtures when natural light is available)? & Lgt & 0 of 45 & all three & Daylight harvesting needs a photosensor, i.e. illuminance, which the lighting stream includes (`lighting power, lighting status, or illuminance'). \\
E09 & Variable air volume (VAV) system? & ActC+\allowbreak{}ActP & 16 of 45 & all three & BAS-controlled VAV boxes carry damper command and position or airflow. \\
E10 & Does the building automation system control ... lighting? & Lgt & 0 of 45 & all three & A BAS that commands lighting holds the lighting on/\allowbreak{}off status (the lighting stream includes lighting status). \\
E11 & Dedicated outside air system (DOAS)? & none & — & no stream & No stream assumed; a dedicated outdoor-air system need not measure outdoor-air flow. \\
E12 & Economizer cycle? & OAT & 39 of 45 & enriched (strong) & An economizer's high-limit control cannot decide when to use outside air without sensing outdoor-air temperature or enthalpy (90.1 \S{}6.5.1). \\
E13 & District chilled water /\allowbreak{} district steam or hot water used? & Sub & 22 of 45 & enriched (strong) & District energy is sold by metered quantity, so a thermal-energy revenue meter exists, as the electricity utility meter does; the end-use submeter stream includes thermal energy. \\
E14 & Central chillers used for cooling? /\allowbreak{} BAS controls cooling? & Run+\allowbreak{}Load & 28 of 45 & enriched (moderate to strong) & A BAS that commands a chiller plant reads whether it runs and what it delivers (chilled-water temperatures or flow). \\
E15 & Boilers used for heating? /\allowbreak{} BAS controls heating? & Run+\allowbreak{}Load & 28 of 45 & enriched (moderate to strong) & A BAS that commands a heating plant reads whether it runs and what it delivers (hot-water temperatures or flow). \\
E16 & BAS controls heating or cooling? & SpC & 1 of 45 & enriched (moderate) & Occupied/\allowbreak{}unoccupied scheduling is a BAS's most basic function, so a scheduled setpoint exists apart from the setpoint in effect; whether it is kept as its own point varies by system. \\
E17 & Demand responsive lighting (reduces lighting at times of peak demand)? & Lgt & 0 of 45 & enriched (moderate) & Dimming lights on a utility signal requires networked lighting control that knows the lighting state. \\
E18 & VRF system? & T+\allowbreak{}Sp+\allowbreak{}Run & 19 of 45 & enriched (moderate) & A variable-refrigerant-flow (VRF) central controller reports indoor-unit temperature, setpoint and run state (`don't know' counted as no). \\
E19 & Chiller or boiler plant, with a BAS that controls heating or cooling? & Pwr & 21 of 45 & optimistic only (weak) & Chiller or boiler input power is often integrated into the BAS, but not reliably. \\
E20 & Formal energy management plan in which energy targets are set and consistently monitored? & Sub & 22 of 45 & sensitivity only (weak) & A plan with monitored targets suggests some end-use monitoring, but targets can be tracked from utility bills alone. \\
\end{longtable}
\vspace{-0.5\baselineskip}\noindent\parbox{\textwidth}{\scriptsize Declaring: how many of the reference set's 45 knowledge graphs declare every stream of the row. Use: all three = the primary result and the strict and enriched scenarios; the strict scenario removes, from the automation-system routes, every stream that fewer than a tenth of the knowledge graphs declare. In parentheses: the row's grade, how strongly the equipment implies the stream, set before any effect was computed. Reasoning: the row's assumption; the full wording, with its sources, is deposited with the data and code.}\par
